text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Filmnet, a satellite network that Croatia joined as a sixth member in October 1996, will be terminated at the end of the month after French firm Canale Plus buys it.
- Jadran Film production company director, Zdravko Mihalic, sacked following a vote of no confidence from the supervisory board.
- By the year 2010 two hydroelectric power plants to be built, one to the north and the other to the south of Zagreb, according to a new energy plan for the capital.

- Interview with Zlatko Canjuga, president of the ruling party committee in Zagreb: The Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) represents a barrier against neosocialism and the destabilisation of Zagreb and Croatia.
- Some 330 tonnes of crude and 26,000 cubic meters of gas are produced daily on INA's oilfields in Djeletovci area under UNTAES control.

- Croatian authority with all the institutions will be established in the municipalities in Eastern Slavonia after the April 13 election regardless of whether local Serbs are given the six municipalities they are requesting, the deputy president's chief-of-staff, Vesna Skare-Ozbolt, says in an interview.
- A joint Croatian-Italian committee meets to discuss payment of $35 million in war reparations to Italy.
- Two post offices and an exchange bureau robbed in Zagreb over the weekend. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
